subject: GDPR role mapping & export paths — POC contract coordination
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@horizonhealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: devops@horizonhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: GDPR: role mapping + export path scoping for POC

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As Horizon prepares supplier-side checks for the POC, legal asked that we confirm two things before we move to signature:

1) Role mapping — we need a short statement whether Redwood will be a processor or joint controller for the POC workloads (the product team needs this clarified for our internal TIA).
2) Export paths — we require an inventory of potential export routes for EU data (hosting region, any routed analytics, and known subprocessors).

We anticipate redlines on the DPA and the SCCs adoption; if you can share a draft role map and any standard text you expect to use for SCCs/fallbacks it will help speed review.

We'd like to close the legal checklist this week if possible — next step for us is to run this with our InfoSec.

Best,
Marta
Marta Lopez
Counsel, Horizon Health
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: GDPR: role mapping + export path scoping for POC

Marta — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps from our side: 

- Role mapping: by default Redwood will act as Processor for the POC data flows. Where customers push training data into a dedicated environment (rare for this POC), that would remain Controller-managed. Laura (cc'd) will confirm language to include in the DPA.

- Export paths: primary hosting region for EU data is frankfurt (eu-central-1). Secondary analytics/backfill routes go through our US analytics cluster (us-west-2) only if explicitly enabled by customers; we can offer an orderform flag to disable analytics forwarding. Subprocessor list is maintained in the Console and we will provide a snapshot export.

I'll ask Laura to attach a redline with suggested controller/processor language and SCCs fallback text. If Horizon can share any specific TIA flags (e.g., KMS/HSM or retention limits) that would be helpful.

Can we aim to exchange redlines tomorrow so legal can review on Tuesday?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: GDPR: role mapping + export path scoping for POC

Marta, Alex — attaching a first-pass redline for Horizon's review. Attachment: Horizon_DPA_Redline_20261121.pdf

Key points in the redline (summary):
- Processor vs Controller: Redwood takes Processor obligations for hosted inference and telemetry. We added a short clarifying sentence in Section 1.1 to avoid ambiguity for the POC. Please confirm whether Horizon will be the data controller for any customer-submitted training sets — if so we will add a narrow carve-out.
- SCCs: we propose adopting the latest EU Commission SCCs (Module Two/Processor addendum path) and included a fallback execution clause referencing our hosted SCC annex.
- Subprocessors & export flows: included commitment to provide a current subprocessor inventory within 5 business days of request and an orderform checkbox to opt out of cross-border analytics.
- Security/KMS: we can commit to customer-provided KMS tokens for key-wrapping of persistent exports; for primary inference KV cache we recommend a managed KMS with audit logging.
- Retention: proposed default 90-day log/telemetry retention for POC; we can shorten to 30 days by orderform if Horizon requires.

Open questions for Horizon (to confirm in reply):
- Do you require HSM-backed key storage for custody of keys used for any backups leaving the EU for analytics.
- Any preferred minimum retention period below 30 days?

Action items I propose:
- Horizon to send any DPA redlines back (we can compare side-by-side).
- Redwood legal to provide a clean role-map spreadsheet (attaching Redwood_Role_Map_v2.xlsx).
- Alex to confirm whether sales should enable the analytics forwarding flag by default for this POC.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Role_Map_v2.xlsx
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@horizonhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T08:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: GDPR: role mapping + export path scoping for POC

Laura, Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround and the role map. Attached is our proposed TIA addendum with a couple of local regulator-driven edits: HH_DPA_TIA_20261122.docx

High-level concerns from Horizon legal/infosec:
- We need explicit HSM commitments for custody of keys used for any backups leaving the EU for analytics.
- We prefer a 30-day default retention for telemetry; please confirm the orderform flag is sufficient contractual protection.
- A small redline to SCC fallback language: if Redwood accepts vendor SCCs, we require a written confirmation step before any cross-border transfer is enabled.

We'll push this through our internal TIA tracker after you confirm whether Redwood can accept the HSM requirement for exported backups. If any of these items are non-starters for Redwood, call that out now so we can flag to procurement.

Best,
Marta
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: GDPR: role mapping & export path scoping — next steps (internal)

Forwarding Horizon's latest with my quick internal ask.

Summary / proposed plan: 
- KMS/HSM: Laura — can Redwood commit to HSM-backed key custody for backups that Horizon designates as "exported backups"? If yes, what is the timeline/cost impact and how should it be surfaced in the orderform (one-time config vs tiered SLA)?
- Retention: confirm we accept 30-day telemetry default for the POC; I'll set analytics-forwarding to off by default until Horizon signs.
- SCC confirmation step: propose we add a single-line workflow in the orderform that requires customer sign-off before any cross-border transfer is toggled on; legal to draft the required confirmation text.

Action items (owners):
- Laura: cost/timeline on HSM commitment + draft confirmation text for SCCs (ETA: 48 hours).
- Alex: update orderform flags and disable analytics-forwarding for HW-2026-0783 (ETA: today).
- Karthik: if there are infra constraints on enabling HSM per-customer, flag any blockers and expected runbook changes (ETA: 24 hours).

Related artifacts: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/97531/HW-2026-0783 (HubSpot) — I'll attach final redline to the deal. DocuSign link will follow for the final DPA.

Thanks — let's converge quickly on the HSM answer; procurement is watching this for an end-of-month close.
